restoration_note: The kephalaion describes the appointed moment when divine operative power (Living Spirit / Molding of Man clothed in Living Fire) presses into the disordered natural and discriminates the natures-of-nature out of the storehouses, leaving them argon (inactive). The chapter is structured around an analogy with the human body: the soul animates the body and its small wellsprings, and when soul departs, the body is dead — likewise when the natures are taken from the storehouses of the Land of Darkness, the storehouses become a dead body, a land without life. Editor restorations were accepted where they sit on this established formulary. The largest unconstrained lacunae (notably {69}, {70}, {41}, {43}, {76}, {78}, {80}, {82}) were left unrestored or marked low: they fall in passages where the comparative formula is repeating but the precise wording cannot be recovered from the visible traces. Morphological completions (ⲛ, ⲙ, ⲟⲛ, ⲃⲁ, ⲧⲏ, ⲓⲟ, ⲧⲁⲙ, ⲧⲟⲓ, ⲧⲉⲛ, ⲏⲧϩ, ⲁ, ⲍ, ⲣⲉⲧϩ) confirm the standing vocabulary of the chapter (ⲧⲁⲙⲓⲟⲛ, ⲥⲧⲟⲓⲭⲉⲓⲟⲛ, ⲉⲛⲉⲣⲅⲓⲁ, ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧϩ, ⲁⲛⲝⲱⲭ).
